root_cause_label: Base model loaded with num_labels=20 creating randomly-initialized classifier head before LoRA adapter application, so merged model has untrained classification weights
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent loaded the base model with num_labels=20 (producing a randomly-initialized classifier head), then applied and merged the LoRA adapter without recognizing that the classification head remained random and was never trained, producing high-confidence but meaningless language detection outputs.
t_err_evidence: base_model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_name, num_labels=20) creates fresh randomly-initialized classifier in saved setup script
t_commit_evidence: Once the script with num_labels=20 is written and the environment issues are resolved, the agent simply runs that script at step 24 without reconsidering the model loading logic; the wrong architecture is locked in from step 13 onward.
t_surface_evidence: Some weights ... were not initialized ... and are newly initialized ... You should probably TRAIN this model
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked understanding that calling AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained with num_labels=20 on a base checkpoint creates a fresh randomly-initialized classification head (the warning confirms this), and that the PEFT LoRA adapter from dominguesm/xlm-roberta-base-lora-language-detection only contains LoRA delta weights for encoder attention layers rather than a replacement classifier head — so the merged model's classification head remained random and untrained.
